header.text: <instructions>Read the passage about bees and wasps.</instructions>

contents.text: Have you ever been stung by a bee or wasp? While wasps are long and thin, bees are round and hairy. Most bees can sting only once. After they sting, they die. Wasps, however, can sting a lot. Unlike bees, wasps hunt other insects. Bees get their food from flowers instead.
<instructions>Based on the text, sort the phrases by whether they describe bees, wasps, or both.</instructions>
Authors often compare and contrast two things in their writing.
To compare is to show how two things are alike. When authors compare, they often use signal words such as like, same, both, also, and too.
To contrast is to show how two things are different. When authors contrast, they often use signal words such as unlike, different, only, but, and while.
